title: Feature Request: Break Intervals by Day Change
description:
Haven't found a feature request possibility, so I decided to create an issue; hope you don't mind. 

I would like to know if there's a function which splits intervals by "_calendar day boundaries_". 

**Example** 

I would like 

>```none
> > iv(X$start_time, X$end_time)
><iv<datetime<local>>[1]>
>[1] [2025-08-30 20:00:00, 2025-08-31 02:00:00)
>```

to be split into 

>```none
> > iv(X$start_time, X$end_time)
><iv<datetime<local>>[2]>
>[1] [2025-08-30 20:00:00, 2025-08-30 23:59:59) # 2025-08-31 00:00:00?
>[2] [2025-08-31 00:00:00, 2025-08-31 02:00:00)
>```

(This is manually created.)

**Reprex:** 

>```none
> > dput(iv(X$start_time, X$end_time))
>structure(list(start = structure(1756576800, tzone = "", class = c("POSIXct", 
>"POSIXt")), end = structure(1756598400, tzone = "", class = c("POSIXct", 
>"POSIXt"))), class = c("ivs_iv", "vctrs_rcrd", "vctrs_vctr"))
>```

If it's already there, please delete. 

Haven't found `{dplyr}`-implementations besides [this](https://stackoverflow.com/a/77718983/20002111) from SO, which isn't vectorised due to use of `seq()`. Simple modifications to obtain a base `R` version for breaks at midnight: 

```r
splitByDate = function(s, e,  o=24*60L^2L) {
  # https://stackoverflow.com/a/77718983/20002111
  is.POSIXct = \(p) inherits(p, 'POSIXct')
  stopifnot(all(is.POSIXct(c(s, e))))
  b = seq.POSIXt(trunc.POSIXt(s, 'day'), trunc.POSIXt(e, 'day') + o, by=o) |>
    c(s, ...=_, e) |>
    pmax(s, ...=_) |>
    pmin(e, ...=_) |>
    unique()
  if (length(b)==1L) {
    start = end = b
  } else {
    start = head(b, -1)
    end = tail(b, -1)
  }
  data.frame(start, end) 
}
```

>```none
> > X = splitByDate(X$start, X$end)
> > X
>                start                 end
>1 2025-08-30 20:00:00 2025-08-31 00:00:00
>2 2025-08-31 00:00:00 2025-08-31 02:00:00
>```

For packages/approaches behaving different than `{ivs}`'s nice right-open interval dogma, one might want to add 

```r
X$end[format(X$end, '%H:%M:%S')=='00:00:00'] = X$end[format(X$end, '%H:%M:%S')=='00:00:00'] - 1L
```

Application: [SO:questions/79629541](https://stackoverflow.com/a/79630732/20002111)

title: ivs doesn't respect multiple items in group_by()
description:
Hello,

I don't have an example I can easily share, but I've discovered that ivs operations (specifically set operations) don't seem to work when there is more than 1 group by level.

For example, group_by(person_id) is fine, but group_by(person_id, location_id) does not work.  It seems to calculate set operations of all rows in the first group level against all other rows.  This isn't what you would expect if it were grouped by multiple levels.

Thanks,

Adam

title: `iv_span()` should have an `infinite` argument
description:
Like `range.default()` - surprisingly `range()` is written in a way that prevents `finite = TRUE` from working on Date vectors

``` r
range(as.Date(c(1, Inf), origin = "1970-01-01"), finite = TRUE)
#> [1] "1970-01-02" "Inf"

range(1, finite = TRUE)
#> [1] 1 1
```

But we could add an `infinite` argument to `iv_span()` that would probably take `c("keep", "drop")`.

If `"drop"` is used then either `start` or `end` could be trimmed in a way that results in an empty vector, so the `infinite` behavior should be handled before `empty` behavior, and we should check _both_ `start` and `end` for emptiness, rather than just `start` as we do now.

If `"drop"` is used then we'd use `is.infinite()` to detect infinite values and just hope that it works in a mostly generic way. It seems to error if it isn't implemented rather than returning something weird

```r
> is.infinite(data.frame(x=1:5))
Error in is.infinite(data.frame(x = 1:5)) : 
  default method not implemented for type 'list'
```

See also https://github.com/tidyverse/tidyr/issues/1496

title: Match-like functions should allow data frames where the last column is an iv
description:
For example, `iv_locate_overlaps()` is useful, but often you want to group by some additional fields. For example, you might want to compute overlaps _within_ each state. For genomic data, it is useful to compute overlaps _within_ a chromosome (this is what GenomicRanges is all about).

We could support this in ivs by allowing functions that take `needles` and `haystack` to be able to handle data frames where the first `n-1` columns are columns to group on using equality, and the `n`th column is an iv where the conditions are controlled by `type`. Anything more complicated than this would require dropping down to `vec_locate_matches()` directly.

The current alternative is to nest the iv column in each data frame by the groups, join the tables on the groups, and then map `iv_locate_overlaps()` over the two list columns of nested iv vectors.

In the long term, this will be easily accomplished with dplyr non-equi joins, but I think it would still be useful for ivs to support this for lower level programmatic overlaps.

The functions that take a single iv, like `iv_groups()`, don't need to support this because they work naturally with `group_by()` already. Neither do the pairwise functions, because they require parallel iv vectors, not vectors from different tables.


---

Hmm, in theory it would apply to set operations too? That might be tricky because the underlying implementations don't support groups natively

title: `iv_between()` (and friends) variant that returns a vector the size of `haystack`
description:
Like https://stackoverflow.com/questions/74874828/identify-intervals-where-a-given-vector-of-dates-occurs

i.e. you want to return `TRUE` if a `haystack[i]` interval contained any of the `needles` vector. Another way to say it is: if any of the `needles` were between `haystack[i]`, return `TRUE`.

Right now it is: if `needles[i]` is between any of the `haystack` intervals, return `TRUE`, giving us something the size of `needles`.

title: Consider doing missing value propagation before comparison check in `iv()`
description:
Also affects `iv_diff()`

We probably need to do this because `vec_compare()` can "early exit" if it can determine the comparison value early on. This can cause some confusing errors since we normally say that incomplete rows are going to be propagated as missing rows in the result, and I think that should take precedence over the comparison.

``` r
library(ivs)
library(vctrs)

# Can determine comparison early on
start <- data_frame(x = 1, y = NA)
start
#>   x  y
#> 1 1 NA

end <- data_frame(x = 0, y = 2)
end
#>   x y
#> 1 0 2

iv(start, end)
#> Error in `iv()`:
#> ! `start` must be less than `end`.
#> ℹ `start` is not less than `end` at locations: `c(1)`.

#> Backtrace:
#>     ▆
#>  1. └─ivs::iv(start, end)
#>  2.   └─rlang::abort(message) at ivs/R/iv.R:184:4

iv_diff(vec_c(start, end))
#> Error in `iv()` at ivs/R/diff.R:100:2:
#> ! `start` must be less than `end`.
#> ℹ `start` is not less than `end` at locations: `c(1)`.

#> Backtrace:
#>     ▆
#>  1. └─ivs::iv_diff(vec_c(start, end))
#>  2.   └─ivs::iv(start, end) at ivs/R/diff.R:100:2
#>  3.     └─rlang::abort(message) at ivs/R/iv.R:184:4

# Can't determine comparison because of `NA`
start <- data_frame(x = NA, y = 3)
start
#>    x y
#> 1 NA 3

end <- data_frame(x = 0, y = 2)
end
#>   x y
#> 1 0 2

iv(start, end)
#> <iv<data.frame<
#>   x: double
#>   y: double
#> >>[1]>
#> [1] [NA, NA)

iv_diff(vec_c(start, end))
#> <iv<data.frame<
#>   x: double
#>   y: double
#> >>[1]>
#> [1] [NA, NA)
```

title: Provide `vec_ptype()` method for iv
description:
For performance

```r
vec_ptype.iv <- function(x, ...) {
  start <- .subset2(x, 1L)
  start <- vec_ptype(start)
  new_bare_iv(start, start)
}
```

Since currently `vec_ptype()` will do `vec_slice(x, NULL)` which is fairly slow.

``` r
library(ivs)
library(dplyr)
library(vctrs)

set.seed(123)

n <- 125000

id <- sample(seq_len(n), size = n * 5, replace = TRUE)
indices <- vec_locate_sorted_groups(id)$loc

start <- as.Date("2020-01-01") + sample.int(365, size = n*5, replace = TRUE)
end <- start + sample(1:100, size = n*5, replace = TRUE)
iv <- iv(start, end)

chunks <- vec_chop(iv, indices)

system.time({
  list_unchop(chunks)
})
#>    user  system elapsed 
#>  24.335   0.206  24.862

vec_ptype.iv <- function(x, ...) {
  start <- .subset2(x, 1L)
  start <- vec_ptype(start)
  ivs:::new_bare_iv(start, start)
}

system.time({
  list_unchop(chunks)
})
#>    user  system elapsed 
#>  12.272   0.030  12.335
```

title: requirement for iv subclass (non rcrd type)
description:
I'm wanting to build an age based interval vector and it makes sense to do this on top of {ivs}. I need this to work with data.table though so I'm considering building on top of a character vector and dealing with the coercion via `iv_proxy`. 

A rough sketch of the implementation is given below but my question is whether I'm likely to run in to any unforeseen problems due to the class not being a strict subclass (i.e. the class below is `age_iv` not `"age_iv" "iv" "vctrs_rcrd" "vctrs_vctr"`) or should everything (save printing) be handled due to `iv_proxy` and any issues arising I could consider a bug?

Hope this makes sense.

``` r
library(ivs)

new_age_iv <- function(start, end,...) {
    out <- sprintf("[%d, %d)", start, end)
    structure(out, class = "age_iv")
}

iv_proxy.age_iv <- function(x, ...) {
    start <- as.integer(sub("\\[([0-9]+), [0-9]+)","\\1",x))
    end <- as.integer(sub("\\[[0-9]+, ([0-9]+))","\\1",x))
    new_iv(start, end)
}

format.age_iv <- function(x, ...) format(iv_proxy.age_iv(x))

iv_restore.age_iv <- function(x, to, ...) new_age_iv(iv_start(x), iv_end(x))

# seems to work
dat <- new_age_iv(c(1, 7, 5), c(2, 8, 9))
iv_groups(dat)
#> [1] "[1, 2)" "[5, 9)"
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "age_iv"
iv_complement(dat)
#> [1] "[2, 5)"
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "age_iv"
```

title: Complete overlap
description:
Inspired by [this SO question](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/73561520/remove-rows-with-overlaped-dates-and-keep-longest-time-interval-in-r-using-dplyr/73561646#73561646). 

It would be nice if it was possible to use `iv_groups` and other grouping functions for **complete** overlapping. 

In the SO question, we have this dataframe:
```r
dat <- structure(list(time_left = structure(c(15191, 15180, 17398, 17398, 
17448, 18048), class = "Date"), time_right = structure(c(15231, 
17410, 17421, 17435, 17454, 18205), class = "Date"), x = c(114, 
20, 10, 1, 5, 100)), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, 
-6L))

   time_left time_right   x
1 2011-08-05 2011-09-14 114
2 2011-07-25 2017-09-01  20
3 2017-08-20 2017-09-12  10
4 2017-08-20 2017-09-26   1
5 2017-10-09 2017-10-15   5
6 2019-06-01 2019-11-05 100
```

Using `iv_identify_groups`, we get groups with only partial overlap, and using `abutting = FALSE` does not make a difference:
```r
df %>% 
  mutate(gp = iv_identify_group(iv(time_left, time_right), abutting = FALSE))

   time_left time_right   x                       gp
1 2011-08-05 2011-09-14 114 [2011-07-25, 2017-09-26)
2 2011-07-25 2017-09-01  20 [2011-07-25, 2017-09-26)
3 2017-08-20 2017-09-12  10 [2011-07-25, 2017-09-26)
4 2017-08-20 2017-09-26   1 [2011-07-25, 2017-09-26)
5 2017-10-09 2017-10-15   5 [2017-10-09, 2017-10-15)
6 2019-06-01 2019-11-05 100 [2019-06-01, 2019-11-05)
``` 

By complete overlap, I mean that both ends of the intervals must be within another one. In this case, we should get only row 3 and 4 grouped together:
```r
df %>% 
  mutate(gp = iv_identify_group(iv(time_left, time_right), complete = TRUE))

   time_left time_right   x                       gp
1 2011-08-05 2011-09-14 114 [2011-07-25, 2017-09-01)
2 2011-07-25 2017-09-01  20 [2011-07-25, 2017-09-01)
3 2017-08-20 2017-09-12  10 [2017-08-20, 2017-09-26)
4 2017-08-20 2017-09-26   1 [2017-08-20, 2017-09-26)
5 2017-10-09 2017-10-15   5 [2017-10-09, 2017-10-15)
6 2019-06-01 2019-11-05 100 [2019-06-01, 2019-11-05)
```

That might be harder than I think to code, but it is certainly useful!

title: Calculating elapsed duration when some intervals span only a single day
description:
As a way of getting familiar with ivs, I tried it on an [old stackoverflow problem](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25330745/calculate-duration-omitting-overlapping-dates-in-r). It could nicely solve the problem if the `iv` function supported interval vectors where the `startdate` == `enddate` (the commented-out dates). Would it be possible to allow these interval vectors?

``` r
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(ivs)

# Original example data
dat <- read.table(
  header = TRUE, text =
    "patientnumber rxnumber startdate stopdate
   100 1 1/1/2014 1/5/2014
   100 2 1/1/2014 1/5/2014
   100 3 1/20/2014 1/22/2014
   # 200 4 2/14/2014 2/14/2014
   200 5 2/15/2014 2/20/2014
   300 5 2/19/2014 2/22/2014 
   # 300 6 3/27/2014 3/27/2014
   # 300 7 3/27/2014 3/27/2014 
   300 8 3/27/2014 3/30/2014 
   # 300 9 3/28/2014 3/28/2014"
)

# Calculate the elapsed duration
dat |> 
  mutate(across(c(startdate, stopdate), mdy),
         iv = iv(startdate, stopdate)) |> 
  group_by(patientnumber) |> 
  summarise(group = iv_groups(iv)) |> 
  mutate(days = iv_end(group) - iv_start(group) + 1)
#> `summarise()` has grouped output by 'patientnumber'. You can override using the
#> `.groups` argument.
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#> # Groups:   patientnumber [3]
#>   patientnumber                    group days  
#>           <int>               <iv<date>> <drtn>
#> 1           100 [2014-01-01, 2014-01-05) 5 days
#> 2           100 [2014-01-20, 2014-01-22) 3 days
#> 3           200 [2014-02-15, 2014-02-20) 6 days
#> 4           300 [2014-02-19, 2014-02-22) 4 days
#> 5           300 [2014-03-27, 2014-03-30) 4 days
```

title: Useful example - Tracking rolling enrollment over time
description:
``` r
library(clock)
library(tidyverse)
#> Warning: package 'tidyr' was built under R version 4.1.2
#> Warning: package 'readr' was built under R version 4.1.2
#> Warning: package 'dplyr' was built under R version 4.1.2
library(vctrs)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'vctrs'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:dplyr':
#> 
#>     data_frame
#> The following object is masked from 'package:tibble':
#> 
#>     data_frame
library(iv)

df <- tibble::tribble(
  ~unique_name, ~enrollment_start, ~enrollment_end,
  "Amy",    "1, Jan, 2017",  "30, Sep, 2018",
  "Franklin",    "1, Jan, 2017", "19, Feb, 2017",
  "Franklin",    "5, Jun, 2017",  "4, Feb, 2018",
  "Franklin",   "21, Oct, 2018",  "9, Mar, 2019",
  "Samir",    "1, Jan, 2017",  "4, Feb, 2017",
  "Samir",    "5, Apr, 2017", "12, Sep, 2018"
)

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    enrollment_start = date_parse(enrollment_start, format = "%d, %B, %Y"),
    enrollment_end = date_parse(enrollment_end, format = "%d, %B, %Y"),
    enrollment_start = calendar_narrow(as_year_month_day(enrollment_start), "month"),
    enrollment_end = calendar_narrow(as_year_month_day(enrollment_end), "month") + 1L
  )

df <- df %>%
  mutate(dates = iv(enrollment_start, enrollment_end), .keep = "unused")

from <- iv_start(min(df$dates))
to <- iv_end(max(df$dates)) - 1

month <- seq(from, to, by = 1)

vec_count(month[iv_locate_between(month, df$dates)$needles], sort = "key")
```

title: Idea for `iv_remove()`
description:
For each interval in `x`, setdiff out all the intervals of `y` and return the remaining intervals after the setdiff. Interval 1 of `x` corresponds to the list element 1 of the result.

This is unfortunately extremely slow right now due to all the vctrs overhead required

I'm using this issue as a place to store the idea in case we come back to it later

```r
iv_remove <- function(x, y) {
  y <- iv_merge(y)

  loc <- iv_locate_overlaps(x, y, no_match = 0L)

  indices <- vec_split(loc$haystack, loc$needles)$val

  # Hack because `vec_chop()` can't deal with zeros
  indices <- vec_assign(indices, vec_equal(indices, list(0L)), list(NULL))

  xs <- vec_chop(x)
  ys <- vec_chop(y, indices)

  map2(xs, ys, iv_difference)
}

```
